# core:http_client

HTTP client over `wasi:http` (`core:http_client`).

An `HttpClient` holds what belongs to one origin: the base URL, the headers
every request carries, and the timeouts. `request` sends one request and
answers an `HttpResponse` once its headers arrive; its body is read whole
(`bytes`, `text`, `json`), as chunks (`body`), or as Server-Sent Events
(`events`).

Headers, trailers and the query are name-value pairs in the order given,
written as an object literal (`{ accept: "text/html" }`). A literal cannot
repeat a key, so a name sent more than once is written as a list of pairs
(`[["accept", "text/html"], ["accept", "text/plain"]]`) or built with
`push`.

A status of 4xx or 5xx is a response, not an error. The client follows no
redirect and retries nothing.

See `docs/wep-2026-11-24-core-http-client.md` for the design.

## Synopsis

```wado
struct Item {
    id: i32,
}

// RFC 6761 reserves `.invalid` never to resolve, so this request fails
// before any response.
let client = HttpClient::new("https://api.example.invalid/v1", ClientInit {
    headers: { accept: "application/json" },
}).unwrap();
let result = client.request("/items", RequestInit {
    query: { limit: "10" },
});
match result {
    Ok(mut res) => {
        let items = res.json::<List<Item>>();
        assert res.ok() && items.is_ok();
    },
    Err(e) => {
        assert e matches { Transport([_::Request, _]) };
    },
}
```

### `pub struct RequestInit`

One request, relative to the client's base URL.

#### `method: Method`

Appended after the client's headers; a name in both keeps both values.

#### `pub fn request<P: AsStrSlice>(&self, path: P, init: RequestInit = RequestInit {}) -> Result<HttpResponse, HttpError> with Client`

Send a request for `path`, which starts with `/` and holds no `?` or

#### `pub fn request_streaming<P: AsStrSlice, effect E>(&self, path: P, init: RequestInit, write: fn mut(&StreamWritable<u8>) -> List<[String, String]> with E) -> Result<HttpResponse, HttpError> with (Client, E)`

- ``contract init.body matches { null }, "a streamed request takes its body from `write`"``

`request` with a body `write` streams, called once the send has
started. The trailers it returns follow the body, after those of
`init`, whose `body` must be `null`.

### `pub struct HttpFields`

A header or trailer section: name-value pairs as the host handed them over.
A value is read as a view over those bytes, never copied, except where a
name repeats and RFC 9110 reads its values as one.

_Fields are private._

#### `pub fn header<S: AsStrSlice>(&self, name: S) -> Result<Option<StrSlice>, HttpError>`

- ``contract !name.as_str_slice().eq_ignore_ascii_case("set-cookie"), "Set-Cookie cannot be joined: read it with `headers_all`"``

The value of `name`, compared without regard to ASCII case: its values
joined with `, ` where it repeats, or an error where that is not UTF-8.

#### `pub fn header_bytes<S: AsStrSlice>(&self, name: S) -> Option<ByteSlice>`

- ``contract !name.as_str_slice().eq_ignore_ascii_case("set-cookie"), "Set-Cookie cannot be joined: read it with `headers_all`"``

`header`, as the octets themselves.

#### `pub fn headers_all<S: AsStrSlice>(&self, name: S) -> Result<List<StrSlice>, HttpError>`

Every value of `name`, each a view, in the order they arrived.
